verdict.line: You lose this if it turns into a long skirmish or he stacks Feast; you win it if you close him down before level 6 or catch him off his 9s Rupture cooldown.

brief.thesis: Aatrox owns the opening trades and solo-kill race because his W (Infernal Chains) threatens 825 range and his E (Umbral Dash) heal keeps him topped up through short fights, which is exactly why he holds the lane and solo-kill edge. But Cho'Gath's W (Feral Scream) silence and R (Feast) permanently inflate his health, so every extended skirmish past mid-lane shifts value toward him — that tension is why the head-to-head sits at only 42.8% over 201 games despite the lane edge.

theirWindow.when: W (Feral Scream) is off cooldown and you're close
theirWindow.what: If you're inside his 300 range and commit to a long trade, Feral Scream silences you and cancels your R activation or follow-up Q swings — disengage to range instead of grinding it out once the silence is up.

yourWindow.when: His Q (Rupture) just missed or is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Rupture is a 9s cooldown ground-targeted zone with no other ranged tool behind it, so the moment it's down, dash in with E and chain W immediately — he has nothing to punish the engage or create space with.

start.why: The 42.5% win rate pick at 76.9% pick rate — the extra sustain outlasts Cho'Gath's Vorpal Spikes poke on every auto-trade exchange.

boots.why: 76.2% pick at 47.6% win rate, and the magic resist plus tenacity directly shortens how long Feral Scream's silence locks you out of your own cooldowns.

core.why: Highest-winrate core path listed (46.2% over 13 games) — the ability haste keeps your W/Q cycling faster than his 9s Rupture and 13s Feral Scream cooldowns.
Converts your empowered Q swings into healing on crit, which matters more as his health pool grows from Feast stacks.
Delays the true damage tick from Feast, turning his all-in-or-nothing R into a trade you can actually survive.

situational.when: you're ahead in solo kills and want to close out all-ins before level 6
he's stacked 3+ Feast charges and his base health is starting to tank your sustained DPS
you need the dash-reset to stay on top of him through his E spike procs

runes.keystoneWhy: The 46.3%-picked page (43.8% win rate) stacks adaptive force through exactly the kind of grindy short trades this matchup produces before Feral Scream can punish you for staying too long.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is run in 75.2% of games and converts your early solo-kill advantage into a secured kill before he can out-scale; Flash+Teleport (48.2% win rate, 23.1% pick) is the fallback if you expect the lane to stall into a scaling fight.

playing.title: Open fights with W, not Q
playing.detail: Infernal Chains at 825 range forces him to run or eat the damage twice — land it before he's in Vorpal Spikes auto-range so you dictate the trade distance.

playing.title: Hold range after his W is down
playing.detail: Feral Scream is only 300 range; once he's used it, you have 13 seconds to fight freely without fear of the silence cutting off your R or Q sequence.

playing.title: Count his Rupture cooldown
playing.detail: 9 seconds between casts — if he whiffs or lands it on you, that's your window to dash in with E and commit, since he has nothing else to zone you.

playing.title: Never skip a Deathbringer Stance proc
playing.detail: The empowered auto's heal scales off his max health, which only gets more valuable as his Feast stacks grow — take every free instance of it.

playing.title: Stop extending fights past 4 Feast stacks
playing.detail: Once he's grown enough that the true damage tick threatens a kill, shorten your trades to poke-and-reset instead of full commits.

playing.title: Save R for the kill, not the engage
playing.detail: World Ender fears nearby minions but does nothing to his Rupture range, so pop it to finish a fight you're already winning, not to force one open.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are this brief's own analysis, not sourced data.

stats.opponentTip: Use [E] carefully to avoid being hit with Cho’Gath’s (Q) when in combat. Use your [P] basic attack whenever he is in range. Use your skills whenever they come off cooldown to fight him.
